about: The bytes a typed event payload carries, read into a bytes variable of four bytes, into a record's field and into a whole record whose field is bounded at eight, and read by a guard. The wire spells a byte string as its byte-exact Latin-1 text, each byte the character of that code point, so a byte above 0x7F is written as that character. A value past its bound fails as any assignment does: nothing is written, error.execution is raised (`errors` counts it) and the block ends, so what the block would have written after it is not written either. A character past U+00FF is no byte, so a payload that carries one does not read as its schema: error.execution is raised and nothing is written. What this scenario does not say is what a payload longer than the field's sce:max-size does when it takes a route that writes none of it: an engine whose payload buffer is the bound (C11, Rust without an allocator) refuses it whole at the lift, and the others hold the bound where the bytes are written, as a string's is. Expected values are derived from the byte counts, not observed from a backend.

steps.note: a guard reads the payload's bytes: `ab` is a match
the same length and other bytes is a miss, and === is false
the payload replaces the record field by field
nine bytes do not fit a field of eight: the frame is read first, so the sensor stays 7 as well
four bytes fit a variable of four, and are measured
five bytes do not: the variable is left as it was and the block ends before the size is taken
no bytes at all is a byte string of length zero
a sensor of 200 or more takes the payload whole: the record and the list both hold it
nine bytes do not fit a record taken whole: both are left as they were and error.execution is raised
bytes above 0x7F are read as the bytes their characters spell, in the record and in the list
two bytes above 0x7F are two bytes, not the four of their UTF-8 spelling
a character past U+00FF is no byte: the payload does not read as its schema, error.execution is raised and nothing is written
